entries.title: New Discord members added to name pool
entries.summary: Added JJ, Freshboii, VidTu, DanMizu, and Varocraft25 to the Discord community name pool.
highlights: JJ, Freshboii, VidTu, DanMizu, and Varocraft25 can now appear as item name contributors

entries.title: New Discord member added to name pool
entries.summary: Added anuncommonguy to the Discord community name pool.
highlights: anuncommonguy can now appear as an item name contributor

entries.title: Now available for Minecraft 1.20.1
entries.summary: Adventure Item Names now runs on Minecraft 1.20.1 as well as 1.21.1 — the same procedural item names, provenance lore, themed packs, and in-game naming editor, just on the older version. Fabric and Forge are supported on 1.20.1; NeoForge remains 1.21.1.
highlights: New: Fabric and Forge builds for Minecraft 1.20.1
Same naming engine, lore, bundled themed packs, and in-game editor on both 1.21.1 and 1.20.1
Existing 1.21.1 builds (Fabric / Forge / NeoForge) are unchanged

entries.title: Item naming restored on Minecraft 1.20.1
entries.summary: Several naming paths silently stopped working on Minecraft 1.20.1 after multi-version support landed. Armor from villagers, crafting, and loot now gets named and described on 1.20.1 just like on 1.21.1, and custom or hand-authored datapacks now load correctly instead of being rejected as incompatible.
highlights: Armor (helmets, chestplates, leggings, boots) now gets procedural names on 1.20.1
Custom & hand-authored datapacks now load on 1.20.1 (correct pack format)
Crafted-item descriptions, bow and shield naming now work on 1.20.1

entries.title: New supporter names, plus the Archivist
entries.summary: Nine more Discord supporters join the name pool, and a new Archivist theme runs through place and title names.
highlights: Added 9 Discord supporters: Dot, Lil Detective Crunch, General Efficiency, CorporalJack, Mime, AutisticMime, Pouncing Hen, TJYoungHeng, Nikeeta707.
New place: the Archivist Society.
New title prefixes: Archivist and Detective.

entries.title: 3 new Discord supporters
entries.summary: Three more community members from the Discord join the name pool: mel, banguela, and morpheus the 3 feeted cat.

entries.title: Testificate joins the Minecraft lore names
entries.summary: Added "Testificate" to the Minecraft lore name pool — the name Notch accidentally left on villagers in the Beta 1.9 pre-releases. It can now show up anywhere the mc_lore pool feeds in: mob names, "forged by", weapon titles and more.
highlights: New mc_lore entry: Testificate

entries.title: Supporter name spelling fix: TJYongHeng
entries.summary: Corrected a Discord supporter's name in the community name pool — TJYoungHeng is now spelled TJYongHeng. Generated names that credit them (forged by, mob names, weapon titles) now get it right.
highlights: discord_people pool: TJYoungHeng renamed to TJYongHeng

entries.title: New Discord supporter name
entries.summary: Another community member from the Discord joins the name pool, in five forms: sstasske, Staske, Stas, Stanislav, and Stanislav The Russian.

entries.title: More community names
entries.summary: Nine more members of the Discord community join the name pool, including the players helping tune item trade values. Queen Sppongy, the slimey also arrives as a full name, and Choo Choo joins the random names, so both can turn up in forged by lines, mob names and weapon titles.
highlights: Discord names: Goingforlong, Mr_agah, Collapseofsmth, Kyrielle, Lyraluithin, LitniR, AshSeven, AshSeven7, Ash7
New full name: Queen Sppongy, the slimey
New random name: Choo Choo

entries.title: Repaired items keep their name
entries.summary: Combining two worn items in a crafting grid now keeps the name and description of the left item (or the top one, if they share a column), the same item whose stats are kept. A repair no longer adds a new crafted by line.
highlights: Crafting-grid repairs keep the left item's name and description
Repairing no longer adds a crafted by line

entries.title: Dyed armour credits the dyer
entries.summary: Dyeing leather armour now adds a "Dyed by" line instead of claiming you crafted it. Dyeing it again updates that line rather than adding another, and the original maker's line stays.

entries.title: Procedurally generated mob names
entries.summary: Mobs can now get freshly invented names built from syllables, like Dongik, Miggkle, Kinkleberry and Zimworth, with over 500,000 possible combinations. These names also show up as last names and in item descriptions such as 'Forged by …'. Mob names are now more often a single word.
highlights: New name formula: consonant + vowel (or vowel pair) + optional n/m/s/ng/ff/t/b/d/g/p/ss/gg/bb + an ending like -kle, -worth, -smith, -berry, -sniff or a generated vowel+consonant
About half of mob first names now come from the formula; the hand-written name list still appears
Mob last names now actually appear (4% of mobs), drawing from the formula and the name list
Titles on mob names are rarer (prefix 10% to 4%), so about 90% of mobs get a single-word name
Themed name packs (Wholesome, Minecraft Names, ATLA, etc.) are unchanged

entries.title: More name endings; PlayerMobs keep more player-like names
entries.summary: Generated names get 37 new endings, from -smack and -wink to -wright, -rump and -schmeckle, for about 670,000 possible names. PlayerMobs now use generated names much less often, so they read more like real players, while villagers and other mobs are unchanged.
highlights: 37 new name endings, bringing the list to 65
PlayerMob first names: generated names drop from about half to about 1 in 5
PlayerMob last names: generated names drop from 70% to about 25%
Weights remain adjustable in the in-game chain editor

entries.title: More name sounds
entries.summary: Generated names get 8 new endings, like -athon, -seph, -thrine, -board and -age, and three new vowel sounds (oe, eu, ui), as in Moewitle and Zuiwit.
highlights: New endings: -athon, -seph, -oeseph, -ie, -thrine, -board, -ako, -age (73 in all)
New vowel pairs: oe, eu, ui (14 in all)

entries.title: Shorter editor command
entries.summary: You can now open the name editor with /adventuretimenames config, as well as /adventureitemnames config.

entries.title: Two more name endings
entries.summary: Generated names can now end in -nica or -leighly, as in Hinica and Doleighly.
highlights: New endings: -nica, -leighly (75 in all)

entries.title: Smoother generated names
entries.summary: Generated names no longer pile up vowels where the pieces join, so you won't see names like Zeaik or Bouoeseph any more. Endings that start with a vowel now always follow a consonant, as in Lunom and Zuegitle.
highlights: Vowel-start endings (-ik, -itle, -ock, -om, -athon, -oeseph, -ie, -ako, -age and the generated vowel + consonant endings) only follow a consonant
Names with 3 or more vowels in a row drop from about 6% to none

entries.title: New name sounds
entries.summary: Generated names get the ur and or sounds and a new lt in the middle, as in Kurdock, Jorfoot and Joltsmith.
highlights: New vowel sounds: ur, or (16 in all)
New middle sound: lt (14 in all)

entries.title: New name sound: ks
entries.summary: Generated names can now have a ks in the middle, as in Hakswit, Roksoh and Gaksboard.
highlights: New middle sound: ks (15 in all)

entries.title: 10 new name endings
entries.summary: Generated names can now end in -ria, -laus, -nan, -phine, -uke, -wonder, -na, -ma, -ba and -lard.
highlights: Name endings: 75 consonant-start, 10 vowel-start

entries.title: Longer, more varied made-up names
entries.summary: Generated names sometimes gain a second ending, and very rarely a third. A few now stop short with no ending at all, and names can end in -ly and -ate.
highlights: Second ending on about 1 in 25 names, third on about 1 in 100
New endings: -ly, -ate

entries.title: Smoother made-up names
entries.summary: When a name gets a second or third ending, a vowel sometimes joins the two so it reads more easily, never making a double vowel. Names can now also use -nkle- and end in -umph.
highlights: Joining vowel between endings, only between two consonants
New name parts: -nkle-, -umph

entries.title: New name ending: -slav
entries.summary: Made-up names can now end in -slav.

entries.title: More varied mob names
entries.summary: Mobs and villagers get more invented names, and a few more named after their type or colour. Now and then an invented name starts with a vowel.

entries.title: Hostile mobs can have names
entries.summary: Hostile mobs now have a small chance to spawn with a name, shown above their head.

entries.title: Real names with made-up endings
entries.summary: Some names now start from a familiar first name and grow a made-up ending, like Thomasilag or Rosalynly.

entries.title: Tidier player-like names
entries.summary: Fan tags and number suffixes now only appear on plain player-like names, not on names that already carry a title. Name editors can set any name part to skip when other parts appear.
